messages:
maya: Hey team — customer reports intermittent 401s only from production bundle (webpack + terser). Dev builds work fine. They say unbundled Node server (local) passes auth. Any ideas?

cj: Do we have repro steps or a minimal repo?

maya: Yes, they sent this repro: simple express server that imports our SDK, calls client.chat.completions with an apiKey env var. If they build with webpack (target node) and run the bundle, requests occasionally return 401 from our API.

alex: That screams bundler shimming fetch or polyfills that drop Authorization header. Which SDK entrypoint are they hitting? ESM/CJS mismatch can cause bundlers to pick a browser-targeted build.

samir: Also check package.json exports map. Some bundlers resolve the ./browser or ./module field and that build might include a fetch polyfill.

maya: They shared package.json and webpack config. package.json has "type":"module" and exports: {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" }
}

webpack config: target: 'node', mode: 'production', optimization: { minimize: true }

They bundle node v18 runtime.

cj: Can we see the built bundle snippet where SDK does the request? If bundler replaced global fetch with node-fetch, it might not forward headers when called via new Request(url, { headers }) depending on polyfill.

maya: They pasted the minified call stack showing fetch(...) invoked with Authorization header present in code, but on the wire header is missing. Also saw warning in build about a dependency using a browser field.

alex: Quick repro I use: bundle a tiny script that does: 
```
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await c.generate({ prompt: 'hi' });
```
Bundle with webpack. Run. Compare curl trace vs node bundle tcpdump.

samir: Workarounds: 1) mark our SDK as external in webpack so it's not bundled 2) force the bundler to resolve cjs entry (require) instead of mjs 3) avoid polyfilling fetch (set resolve.fallback or preferBuiltins).

maya: Customer tried externals, that fixed it. But they'd like to ship a single file bundle. Any upstream fixes?

alex: We should audit our published package: ensure our ESM build doesn't ship a browser-targeted fetch shim. If we need a tiny browser fallback, keep it behind a dist/browser entry and not in main exports. Also add an explicit "node" or "node16" conditional in exports so node bundlers pick node-friendly code. Example exports: 
```
{
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
      "import": { "node": "./dist/index.node.mjs", "default": "./dist/index.mjs" },
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
    }
  }
}
```

samir: We should also add a small note in docs: bundlers may replace fetch; recommend keeping SDK external for server-side bundles or set webpack config: 
```
module.exports = {
  externalsPresets: { node: true },
  externals: [ /@redwood\/inference/ ],
  resolve: { preferRelative: false },
  target: 'node16'
}
```

cj: For reproduction / triage: ask customer to run bundle with NODE_DEBUG=request or tcpdump to confirm header stripping. Also request their webpack stats to see which file was pulled for @redwood/inference.

maya: I asked for webpack stats + built bundle slice. They sent a small minified file — we asked them to run `node -e "console.log(require.resolve('@redwood/inference'))"` against the bundle environment.

alex: If require.resolve points at dist/index.mjs even in CJS context, bundler probably rewrote imports. Another trick: add a runtime assertion in our client that throws if Authorization header absent and logs stack (only in non-prod). Could help customers debug silently.

samir: Action items for us: 1) patch package exports to prefer node entry 2) publish a  patch that avoids shipping any browser fetch shim in node builds 3) add a docs note re: externals and webpack.

maya: Customer confirmed externals is an acceptable short-term fix. They asked for a recommended minimal webpack rule they can use to keep single bundle but preserve Authorization: any ideas?

alex: Tell them to disable fetch polyfills: set `resolve.fallback = { "stream": false }` etc depending on polyfill used, or add alias: { 'node-fetch': false } to prevent replacement. But easier: alias @redwood/inference to require the CJS file explicitly: `alias: { '@redwood/inference$': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/index.cjs') }` That forces the cjs entry.

maya: I'll pass that along. Also noted they saw sourcemap warnings pointing at index.mjs which made debugging harder.

cj: We'll schedule a quick patch release with exports fix and publish notes. Also add an entry to support KB and a short repro guide to include when customers report 401-only-in-bundles.

support-bot: Created ticket INF-8342 for packaging patch + docs.

maya: Thanks all — keeping customer updated. If they can share a tiny repro repo we can test the exact bundler behavior and link to the fix.
